payload.headline: Alphabet drops 3.46% to 272.66, into the buy zone; forecasts still falling

summary.thesis: Alphabet's sales and operating margins are still growing, but free cash flow has collapsed and profit forecasts keep falling, so the stock is only reasonable against its own past prices, not against the cash it produces.
summary.decision: Long-term: buy a first small position now that the price is inside the 271.77–277.07 zone set yesterday, and add more only at 234.35. Swing: wait.
summary.act_at: First buy at 272.66; add at 234.35; no more buying above 234.35 after a daily close below 271.77

payload.happening: Alphabet fell 3.46% to 272.66. That puts it inside the 271.77–277.07 price zone that yesterday's note named as its first buy level. It is now below its 20-day (292.2), 50-day (323.76) and 200-day (337.04) averages, and the 20-day and 50-day averages are both falling. Today's news is about products, all confirmed: Gemini can now operate a Mac for the user, AI chats are going onto the Google homepage, and Blue Origin will launch Google's AI server satellites in 2029. A report that large school districts are thinking about dropping Google Search is still unconfirmed. There is no earnings date in the data.
payload.business: The core business is still growing. Sales rose 24.65% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, faster than the 21.79% two quarters ago. The operating margin (profit from normal operations, as a share of sales) improved to 33.32% from 32.19%. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow (cash left after paying for operations and investment) fell to 19.7B over the last 12 months, down from 73.6B, which is only 4.19% of sales. The company's filings data shows each dollar invested now earns 24¢ a year, down from 40¢ three years ago, so the heavy spending is not paying back yet. Reported profit (a 50.03% net margin) is lifted by one-off gains, and analysts have cut this year's earnings forecast by 5.2% in 30 days. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash (cash and investments minus debt) is 139.0B. Today's headlines mainly affect sentiment. The Gemini and homepage AI launches show the company still competing hard in AI. The school-district report touches search demand, but it is unconfirmed and small next to 471.1B of yearly sales. Nothing today puts demand or the balance sheet at risk. What is at risk is how long cash flow takes to recover.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: what future cash is worth in today's money) gives 25.86 to 69.6 per share, with 51.06 in the middle. That is far below 272.66, because the model starts from only 19.7B of free cash flow. Faster growth barely closes the gap: even 30% starting growth only lifts the value to 77.74. So the cash base, not the growth rate, drives the difference. Compared with its own past, the stock looks fair. The price-to-sales ratio (market value divided by yearly sales) is 7.2, at the 54th percentile of its last 5 years. On that basis the range is 234.35, 282.31 and 375.22, and 272.66 sits just under the 282.31 middle. Compared with similar companies, it looks expensive: peers trade at a median of 4.9 times sales. The price-to-earnings ratio is 14.3 on past profit and 18.2 on next year's forecast. The higher figure on next year shows that analysts expect earnings to fall from 19.56 this year to 14.97 next year once the one-off gains drop out. The fair-value range below uses the own-history method. It holds only if cash flow recovers.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the earlier 73.6B once the current spending cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 24.65% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 21.79% two quarters ago.
The operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%, so growth is not coming at the cost of profitability.
Net cash of 139.0B and a price below the 282.31 own-history middle give room to absorb a slow recovery in cash flow.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, which puts the cash-flow value at 51.06 per share, far below the price.
This year's earnings forecast was cut 5.2% in 30 days, and analysts expect earnings to fall to 14.97 next year from 19.56 this year.
The stock trades at 7.2 times sales against a peer median of 4.9, and is below its 200-day average of 337.04.

levels.what: Today's close, inside the 271.77–277.07 zone and below the 282.31 own-history middle. First, small buy.
Bottom of the zone. A daily close below it means no more buying above 234.35.
Low end of the own-history range. This is the add level, because it leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.

longterm.why: The price has reached the zone that yesterday's plan set for a first buy, and it is now below the own-history middle. The position stays small because cash flow has not recovered and forecasts are still falling.

swing.why: A stop below 271.77 would be too easy to hit, and there is no support level in the data below the zone. No trade until a daily close back above 277.07, with a first target of 293.72.

decision.timing: There is no earnings date in the data, so price levels and forecast changes set the timing. Put open interest (outstanding put contracts) is heaviest at the 290.0, 280.0 and 275.0 strikes, and the put/call open-interest ratio is 1.24, so further pressure around the zone would not be surprising.

change_mind: A daily close below 271.77 cancels further buying above 234.35.
If this year's earnings forecast falls further below 19.56, or next year's falls below 14.97, the next buy moves down to 234.35.
If the next filing shows free cash flow rising above 19.7B, the cash-flow case improves, and adding above 234.35 would be reconsidered.
payload.what_changed: Changed: the long-term action moves from wait to buy, because the price fell to 272.66, inside the 271.77–277.07 zone that yesterday's note set as the first buy level.
